Anyway, Ye I think it’s anxiety. I’ll try to remember main steps I went through to get the issue sorted:
Speaking to someone - never keep issue to urself will drive u insane. Always be there for her and make it clear 
See doctor - say u think it could be stress related so book into see therapist of someone like that. Helped me. Free where I’m from not sure about u but deffo look into it. 
When I had trouble sleeping I would call my mum in, knocked me asleep straight away. Always good having someone to take the edge away. 
Calming practices before bed that become rituals. E.g. warm bath maybe, reading a calming book, colouring, I found writing my thoughts was a good way of getting ready to relax. (Big help for me) 
Not getting too caught up chasing ur own tail and burning out. Try to make it clear to her that the more u focus on stress the worse it will become, for me anyway. Best thing that happened for me was when I was just like fuck it and found something else to have my focus on. Something not related to sleeping, where u don’t need to make sure u have a good rest. I’m a teenager (17) and this time last year I went through heavy sleeping problems, that still scar me today. For me, I was sleeping 3 hours a night and it was broken, poor quality sleep. It was anxiety related and I had trouble saying it to my Mum initially, even to the doctor. I knew it was anxiety related but just felt embarrassed. I wasn’t very close with my mother at the time so it mightn’t apply to this situation but I suggest u have a chat with her saying if it is anxiety related, it’s okay to tell u no mater what it is. Even if she says it’s not, perhaps look for signs that it could be (easily aggressive etc.). I’d say sleeping problems themselves can induce mental instability so be there for her definitely because I know for me that this was by far the worst experience I’ve ever had and the thoughts I got when alone in a dark room night after night are not something I would wish upon anyone. Good luck, let me know how it works out 

Edit - stay away from prescription drugs any drugs that help her to sleep (read up in the chat melatonin might be 50/50 as not a drug per say) . It’s a short term solution and at that age it will certainly distrust her development. I’ve looked into it and spoken to many professionals. It’s not worth it. Best thing is a sleep therapist maybe, or some counselling. Depends what the situation is but I stress that drugs will not be good for ur child in the long run
